sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Zutphen, on the IJssel, charges for parking across its medieval centre and is thinking about taking cars out of it. The council adopted the parking-tax ordinance for 2026 on 15 December 2025, to apply from 1 January 2026; it sets the cost of an additional assessment for unpaid parking tax at 82.00 euros and does not say whether the unpaid tax is added on top [0]. The direction of travel is set in older papers. A framework note for the 2023-2026 inner-city programme states the aim of reducing the number of car parking places in the inner city substantially, with three large car parks at its edge as the starting point and visitors directed to those at the station, Polsbroek and Houtwal; the file carries no adoption or vote [8]. An executive paper of January 2022 lists measures including the abolition of about 23 parking places in characteristic parts of the centre, mostly permit-holder places, and about 280 bicycle spaces at the edges of the shopping area, and we could not confirm they were carried out [9]. On 26 May 2025 a councillor of Burgerbelang proposed in an amendment to the draft Omgevingsvisie to replace the three central facilities with a network at strategic locations, to stimulate garages within or at the edge of the centre and to cut street spaces only once replacements exist; we found no vote on it [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The rest of the news is charging. On 12 June 2023 the executive designated charge-only bays at ten new public posts, with a second bay at nine of them only once the post uses at least 1,750 kWh a year [11]. A decision dated 26 May 2025 does the same for 27 listed locations, and the decision lapses for a location not carried out by 31 May 2027 [12]. A municipal policy rule on charge posts on public land has been in force since 22 August 2024 [13]. The P+R car park at the station, in the Noorderhaven district, was reported as newly completed in March 2017 with 375 car spaces and more than 600 bicycle spaces [6].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The 2026 tariff table sets 3.10 euros an hour at locations including Groenmarkt, Hagepoortplein, Laarstraat, Nieuwstad, Stationsplein and Zaadmarkt, and 2.50 euros at others such as Brasseroord, IJsselkade and Noorderhaven [1]. Long-stay lots are cheaper, 1.95 euros an hour or 11.55 euros a day at Vispoortplein/Houtwal, Roodsplein, Isendoornstraat and Molengracht-west, and 1.05 euros an hour or 3.20 euros a day at the Houtwal lot behind the police station [2]. Rates rose by 5 to 10 cents an hour against 2025, when the first group cost 3.00 euros [3]. An annual resident permit costs 198.60 euros, a second one 321.60, a business permit 649.80 and a visitor pass 40.05 a month, while subscriptions to the pay-and-display lots start at 232.80 euros a year [4]. The council's cost decision for parking fines estimates 2,600 fines at 123.56 euros each, which is a cost estimate and not a usage statistic [5]. The national register lists P+R Lijmerij with Nederlandse Spoorwegen as operator and a tariff of 1.62 euros an hour or 8.11 euros a day, in entries dating from 2021, so they may be out of date; its live feed gives a capacity of 308 where the static record says 375, so the capacity is unclear [7].

Our data cover that park-and-ride for about 57 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 23% on weekdays and 22% at weekends, with a peak of 78% on a Thursday morning. Because the capacity is disputed, treat these as approximate. The paid centre lots are not in our data.
